Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper presents a national-scale spatial land use prediction study focused on Australia’s intensively managed agricultural lands (~85 million ha), covering major production zones from Queensland to Western Australia. While not the entire country, the study area encompasses the dominant agricultural footprint and is treated as a representative national-scale domain for food/fibre production. The primary objective is to simulate future land use change (2013–2050) under 72 scenario combinations involving climate policy, carbon prices, productivity, and adoption rates. It explicitly models competition among 23 existing and 7 new land uses using the LUTO model at ~1.1 km resolution, producing mapped projections of land use transitions (e.g., conversion to carbon plantings, biofuels). The analysis includes quantitative comparisons across multiple scenarios, reports spatially explicit changes in area (e.g., Mha converted), output rates (t/ha, head/ha), and economic returns, and evaluates timing and extent of change. Although biodiversity and carbon sequestration are considered, they are integrated into a land use change framework—not treated as ecological endpoints—thus satisfying inclusion criteria. The study meets all core inclusion requirements: national relevance, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 future scenarios, spatial modeling with quantitative outputs, and mapped projections.)
